title: CRLR/319/2018 of RAJEEV KANNOJIA Vs SMT. CHETNA

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 319 of 2018
Rajeev Kannojia ..........Revisionist
Vs.
Smt. Chetna and others ........ Respondents

Present : Mr. Birendra Singh Adhikari, Advocate for the revisionist.
 Ms. Divya Jain, Advocate for respondent nos.1 and 2.
 Mr. V.K. Jemini, Deputy Advocate General for the State/respondent
 no.3.
JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 The challenge in this revision is made to the
Judgment and Order dated11.07.2018, passed in
Criminal Case No.256 of 2012, Smt. Chetna and another
vs. Shri Rajeev Kannojia, by the court of Additional
Judge, Family Court, Dehradun. By the impugned
judgment and order, an application under Section 125 of
the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short, "the
Code") filed by the respondent no.1, the wife of the
revisionist and the respondent no.2, the son of the
revisionist has been allowed and the revisionist has been
directed to pay `5,000/- per month to each of the
respondent nos.1 and 2 monthly maintenance. The total
maintenance of `10,000/- per month has been allowed.

2
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
peruse the record.
3. The revision was admitted on 05.10.2018 on
that date, as an interim measure, the Court directed the
revisionist to pay `7,000/- to the respondents and stayed
the operation of the impugned order, subject to the final
adjudication of the revision.
4. Learned counsel for the revisionist would
submit that the interim order may be confirmed and
accordingly, the amount of arrears may be reduced from
`10,000/- to `7,000/- per month. He would also submit
that the arrears of the maintenance amount may be
permitted to be paid in easy installments.
5. Learned counsel would also submit that
pursuant to the impugned order of this Court, the
revisionist has been continuously making payment of the
maintenance amount.
6. Learned counsel for the respondent nos.1 and
2 would submit that the amount of maintenance is not on
higher side. She would submit that while upholding the
impugned judgment and order, the revisionist may be
permitted to pay the arrears in installments.

3
7. Impugned judgment and order is quite in
detailed with regard to the financial resources of the
parties. In para 11 of the impugned judgment and order,
the Court recorded the finding with regard to the monthly
income of the revisionist in the month of March, 2012.
According to the impugned judgment, the monthly salary
of the revisionist was `18,133/- (Net), then but, when he
deposed before the court, he has admitted that the salary
then was `40,000/- per month at a basic of `33,000/-.
When the salary was increased? How was it increased?
Annual increments etc., these aspects have not been
examined in the impugned judgment and order.
8. In fact, while assessing the salary of the
revisionist at `18,133/-, the court has observed that, in
fact, the salary of the revisionist is more than that his
gross salary was about `21,000/-. Although, it is the case
of the private respondents that the revisionist was then
receiving `11,000/- as rent of his shop. Even, if it is
assumed that `18,133/- was the net salary of the
revisionist, `10,000/- of maintenance to his wife and son
cannot to be said at higher side.
9. This revision is being decided after a period of
four years. Even during pendency of the case under

4
Section 125 of the Code, when the revisionist deposed
before the court he admitted that his salary then was
`40,000/-.
10. In view of these facts, this Court is of the view
that there appears to be no error in the impugned
judgment and order and the revision deserves to be
dismissed. However, the revisionist may be permitted to
pay the arrears to the respondent nos.1 and 2 in
installments so as to ensure payment of the arrears.
11. The revision is dismissed. Interim order is
vacated. However, the revisionist is at liberty to pay the
arrears of the maintenance in six monthly installments.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 08.06.2022
Sanjay
